newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SORRENTO LEADS FIVE-HOMER ATTACK IN SEATTLE ROUT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SORRENTO LEADS FIVE-HOMER ATTACK IN SEATTLE ROUT.

text.p: Paul Sorrento hit a grand slam and drove in six runs as the Seattle Mariners erupted for 15 hits, including five home runs, in a 14-4 rout of the Milwaukee Brewers on Saturday.
The Mariners halted Milwaukee's nine-game winning streak and their own four-game slide by rocking Brewers rookie starter Steve Woodard.

Woodard (1-1) had one of the greatest debuts in major league history Monday when he struck out 12 and allowed one hit in eight shutout innings as he outdueled Toronto's Roger Clemens. But the Mariners ended his evening early, pounding the 22-year-old for six runs and seven hits in two innings.
Jeff Fassero (10-6) was the beneficiary of the Seattle outburst, allowing two runs and nine hits in six innings.

Sorrento stroked a two-run double in a three-run first and Russ Davis and Ken Griffey homered in the second to stake Seattle to a quick 6-0 lead. Griffey's shot off the right-field foul pole was his 33rd homer of the season.
Griffey made it 8-0 in the fourth with a two-run double off Mike Misuraca, who allowed Sorrento's seventh career grand slam in the sixth inning that increased the lead to 12-0.
Rob Ducey added a solo homer in the sixth and Edgar Martinez hit a solo shot in the eighth off Misuraca.
"We came out and it was a team effort, everybody contributed, everybody had big shots, and that's what it's going to take to win for us down the stretch," Sorrento said.
Jeromy Burnitz hit a two-run homer in the eighth for Milwaukee.
In Kansas City, Dean Palmer homered twice and drove in four runs to pace a five-homer attack as the Royals handed the Boston Red Sox a 10-3 payback for Friday's 10-3 loss.

Chili Davis and Palmer hit back-to-back round-trippers on consecutive pitches in the second inning to forge a 2-2 tie and Mike Macfarlane led off the third with a homer to give the Royals the lead for good.
Palmer added an RBI single later in the third and a two-run homer in the fifth. Yamil Benitez belted a three-run shot, also in the fifth, to complete the long-ball outburst.
Aaron Sele (10-8) was tagged for four runs and five hits in 2 2/3 innings. Tim Belcher (11-9) got the win.

In New York, Paul Molitor homered off the top of the left-centre field fence to break a sixth-inning tie and Rich Becker belted a two-run shot in the seventh to lift the Minnesota Twins to a 5-4 victory over the Yankees.
Scott Stahoviak also homered for Minnesota, making a loser out of David Cone (11-5), who allowed five runs and six hits with three walks and 10 strikeouts in seven innings.
Bernie Williams had three hits for the Yanks, including a home run in the eighth off Greg Swindell (7-2), who picked up the win in relief.

In Oakland, Mike Bordick homered and drove in five runs against his former team and Mike Mussina overcame a shaky start to pitch seven effective innings as the Baltimore Orioles routed the Athletics 13-3.
Chris Hoiles and Brady Anderson hit solo homers for the Orioles, who won for the 10th time in 12 games and extended their AL East lead over second-place New York to six games.
Bordick hit a two-run homer in the third off Carlos Reyes (3-3), added a two-run single in the sixth for a 6-3 lead, and a sacrifice fly in the ninth for a 12-3 advantage.
In Detroit, Paul Quantrill's throwing error allowed Brian Hunter to score the go-ahead run the eighth and Tony Clark had four hits as the Tigers edged the Toronto Blue Jays 8-7.

Hunter lined Quantrill's 3-2 pitch into right field for a double. Bobby Higginson then hit a comebacker to Quantrill, who overthrew third baseman Ed Sprague trying to catch Hunter, who scored, snapping a 7-7 tie.
Doug Brocail (3-4) allowed an unearned run and two hits in the eighth inning for the win. Quantrill (4-4) took the loss.
At Texas, John Smiley won his first start for Cleveland and Jim Thome hit a three-run homer in the sixth inning to lift the Indians to a 7-3 victory over the Rangers.
Smiley (1-0), who was acquired Thursday from the Cincinnati Reds, gave up three runs and five hits in seven innings, walking one and striking out six.
With the game tied 3-3 in the sixth, Thome drove Bobby Witt's 1-0 pitch over the centre-field wall for his 29th home run and a 6-3 lead.
In Anaheim, Dennis Springer allowed four hits over eight innings and Garret Anderson hit a two-run homer as the red-hot Angels beat the Chicago White Sox 5-2.
Springer (7-4) set down the first 11 batters of the game and allowed just two singles and two doubles.
Anderson connected against White Sox starter Chris Clemons (0-1) in a five-run second inning.
The win was the 18th in 24 games for the Angels, who drew within 1 1/2 games of the Yankees for the AL wild-card spot.
